Article Title: In 2012, California professor Yaser Abu-Mostafa opened Caltech’s full machine-learning class online for free; its lectures have drawn more than 8 million views
Article Text:
Caltech professor Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa. Image credits: Wikipedia

Caltech broadcast its first complete course online in 2012

The 18 lectures covered key machine-learning concepts

Beckman institute auditorium at Caltech. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The course continues to reach learners online

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 2012, Caltech professor Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa made his complete machine-learning course available online for free, giving people around the world access to the same class at the California Institute of Technology. The course, named Learning From Data: Introductory Machine Learning Course, was Caltech’s first-ever live broadcast of a full course. The lectures of this course have received more than 9 million views on YouTube and other servers, as mentioned on the official course site. According to the course page on Caltech’s website, the course was built from recordings of the lectures broadcast live in April and May 2012. According to the course page , the course has 18 lectures of about 60 minutes each, plus Q&A sessions that let online viewers take part. The content is organized as a topic-by-topic video library for self-learners.Caltech announced the course in a March 30, 2012 news release , with the live lectures starting on April 3. Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa, a professor of electrical engineering and computer science at Caltech, delivered them as part of his usual teaching. The online course was meant to serve learners who could not be present at the Caltech campus to attend the class there.The material and the level of teaching stayed the same as in the on-campus course. What changed was the delivery: Abu-Mostafa adapted the class for online viewers, including live Q&A with the online audience. In an interview conducted on September 21, 2012, with Caltech’s ENGenious, he stated that the availability of the entire course was an opportunity for people to take a Caltech class. Lectures were provided through iTunes U, YouTube and Caltech’s server. According to the interview in Caltech’s ENGenious magazine , the course had more than 60,000 subscribers on iTunes U alone.Learning From Data introduced the students to both theory and practice of machine learning. The course page lists topics such as linear models, neural networks, support vector machines, regularisation, validation and kernel methods. Among other issues were such notions as overfitting, sampling bias and Data snooping. This enabled the students to understand how the machine-learning systems learn from examples and how their performance is evaluated.One can also comprehend why the system, which operates perfectly on training data, can fail when encountering new data. The course page lists eight homework sets and a final exam and it asks students to know basic probability, matrices and calculus beforehand. The knowledge of probability, matrices and calculus was supposed to be acquired by the students prior to watching the classes. This made the web course more than just a set of introductory videos. The learners were able to go through the lessons and do the corresponding homework and assignments and the Q&A sessions gave the viewers an opportunity to participate in the process of learning during the lecture.According to the official website of the course, there are currently more than 9 million views on YouTube and other servers. The 9 million views represent views of videos and not individual students who have taken the course. The virtual library lets learners access individual topics on their own schedule. They get an opportunity to go back and forth and learn from the available course materials. The idea of Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa broadcasting the whole class ensured that learners who were not at Caltech could access the class taught at the Institute. The fact that the class is still accessible ensures that learners will continue accessing it even many years down the line. It was originally a classroom broadcast that was added in 2012. It has since grown into an online educational platform for those interested in understanding machine learning.
Article Summary: In 2012, Caltech professor Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa made his machine-learning course available online for free. The course, named Learning From Data: Introductory Machine Learning Course, was Caltech’s first-ever live broadcast of a full course. The lectures have received more than 9 million views on YouTube.

Article Title: In 2024, off California, scientists detected 10 DDT+ compounds in deep-sea fish near Catalina, then analysed 215 fish and sediment to examine a possible link between seafloor pollution and marine cont
Article Text:
AI Representation: California scientists found DDT+ chemicals in deep sea fish near Catalina. Image credits: Chatgpt

,

Researchers detected 10 DDT+ compounds in deep-sea fish

Chemical findings pointed to a possible connection between sediment and fish

Little Gibraltar and Cabrillo harbour on Catalina Island. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier research connected fish contamination with polluted ocean sediments

Industrial waste dumped into the ocean can remain in the marine environment long after disposal stops. This has been a concern in Southern California, where decades of industrial activity left behind chemical pollutants, including DDT. More than 50 years after offshore dumping ended, scientists are still investigating how these substances affect marine life. The presence of several DDT-associated chemicals was confirmed by researchers studying deep-sea fish and sediment of Catalina Island in 2024. According to the study in Environmental Science & Technology Letters the research team collected 215 fish from the water column above the San Pedro Basin, around Dumpsite 2. According to their results, 10 DDT+ chemicals were detected in marine organisms, whereas 15 were detected in the nearby sediment. Researchers found an association between DDT chemicals in deep-sea sediment and their presence in marine organisms, but the study did not determine how the chemicals move from the sediment into the food web.The findings appeared in 2024 in Environmental Science & Technology Letters in a research paper examining DDT+ contamination in deep-ocean sediment and marine life in the Southern California Bight.Researchers used chemical analysis to examine sediments and marine organisms from the Southern California Bight, focusing on the San Pedro Basin near the historical offshore dumping area. The researchers conducted their analysis using 215 fish from three species, namely: Cyclothone acclinidens, Melanostigma pammelas and Leuroglossus stilbius. The 215 fish were pooled into four composite samples for chemical testing: 61 shallower and 146 deeper C. acclinidens, six M. pammelas and two L. stilbius. In this study, 10 DDT+ were found in the biota, while 15 were found in the sediments.DDT+ is the broader group. It covers the DDT-related compounds that are routinely tested for, plus TCPM and other lesser-known DDT-related chemicals. Of the DDT+ found in the biota, there were 8 DDT-related and 2 TCPM (tris(4-chlorophenyl) methane) related. All 10 DDT+ compounds found in the biota were also present in the sediment, which brings the total to 15. Of those 15, 13 (87%) had already been identified in Southern California’s birds and marine mammals.The researchers analysed fish obtained at various depths in order to determine the pattern of contamination in the marine environment. C. acclinidens and M. pammelas were collected between 546 and 784 meters, while L. stilbius was collected between 546 meters and the surface. Within that range, the C. acclinidens composite from the shallower layer (546 to 657 meters) had less total DDT+ than the composite from the deeper layer (657 to 784 meters). But both the TCPM-associated compounds were not detected in the surface-dwelling L. stilbius sample. These data do not show any consistent correlation between depth and contamination for all three fishes.TCPMs were found in every biota sample except the single L. stilbius composite, which contained neither of the two TCPM-related compounds. As these compounds were also found in deep ocean sediments, it was concluded that the seafloor could be one of the sources of contaminants getting into the marine food web. However, the exact pathway by which the compounds were transferred from sediments to fish was not determined in this study.A separate 2024 study, “The persistent DDT footprint of ocean disposal, and ecological controls on bioaccumulation in fishes”, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in November 2024, examined existing sediment and fish contamination data collected across Southern California. It was established that the closer the fish were to the regions with high concentrations of DDT in sediment, the higher the level of accumulation of the compound in fish. As demonstrated in the above-mentioned study, the consequences of past activities are still present in the marine ecosystem in the region, more than 50 years after the last industrial discharge in 1971. From the results of these studies, it can be stated that the deep-sea sediments are still one of the components of pollution of the waters of Southern California. Even though the process of movement of DDT+ compounds up the food chain is not yet entirely clear, the presence of the compound in both the sediment and marine organisms proves that its effects are still present. The PNAS paper compiled a database of decades of sediment and fish measurements. It found that DDX levels in fish rose with sediment contamination, though not in a simple, uniform way. The authors say ecological factors such as species and habitat use mattered only in context and that combining ecotoxicology with ecology will be needed to predict risk in undersampled regions and species.
Article Summary: Researchers found 10 DDT+ compounds in deep-sea fish near Catalina Island. 15 DDT+. compounds were also found in the nearby sediment. Researchers found an association between DDT chemicals in sediment and their presence in marine organisms, but the study did not determine how the chemicals move from the sediment into the food web.

Article Title: A California school district was ordered by a jury to pay $29 million to a former elementary pupil who alleged years of abuse by a teacher; six related lawsuits involving the same educator are still p
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A school is meant to be a place where children are protected, but a former elementary pupil in California has spent years seeking accountability for abuse he says he suffered inside a classroom. His civil case against ABC Unified School District has now resulted in a $29 million jury award, making it the first of seven lawsuits involving allegations against the same former teacher to reach trial. The verdict, announced by the plaintiff's lawyers on November 5, has brought renewed attention to claims that the district knew about the educator's alleged misconduct involving other students but failed to act. Six related cases are still pending.The plaintiff, identified in court-related publicity only as J.O., attended Luther Burbank Elementary School in Artesia, California. According to an announcement issued by his legal team at Herman Law, he alleged that he was sexually abused by a teacher when he was a child. The lawsuit accused ABC Unified School District of failing to protect students despite having prior notice of the teacher's alleged sexual misconduct involving other pupils.The case was tried by Herman Law attorneys Greg Glazer and Justin Felton. The jury awarded J.O. $29 million, according to the firm, which announced the result through a November 5 press release. The lawyers said the case was the first of seven involving allegations against the same former teacher to go before a jury. Six other cases have yet to be tried.The allegations raise questions not only about the conduct of the former educator but also about the responsibility of school authorities when concerns about an employee's behaviour emerge. The plaintiff's central argument was that the district had information about alleged misconduct involving other students and did not take adequate steps to prevent further harm. The claims against the district therefore focused on its alleged failure to respond to warnings and protect children under its care.However, the $29 million figure needs an important qualification. A November 9 report by legal publication Daily Journal said ABC Unified had stipulated to negligence and liability shortly before the trial, leaving the jury to determine damages. The publication also reported that the district said it had reached a confidential settlement with J.O. during the trial and, as a result, would not have to pay the jury's $29 million award. The settlement amount and terms have not been made public.The distinction is significant: the jury's award is not necessarily the amount the plaintiff will receive, and the district's account of the settlement should not be confused with the verdict itself. The publicly available announcement from Herman Law did not disclose the settlement. The district's reported position adds a separate development to the case, while the financial terms remain undisclosed.The six remaining lawsuits could now bring further scrutiny to the district's handling of complaints involving the same former teacher. Each case will have to be considered on its own evidence, including the individual plaintiff's allegations and what school officials knew or should have known at the relevant time. The first trial, however, has placed the broader allegations in the spotlight.The teacher has not been publicly identified in the announcement issued by Herman Law. Nor does the release specify the years during which the alleged abuse took place, the plaintiff's age at the time or the precise circumstances in which the district is said to have received earlier warnings.The case comes amid wider scrutiny of how California school districts have dealt with historical claims of sexual abuse. A December 2025 investigation by the Los Angeles Times found that public school districts across the state had faced more than 1,000 lawsuits since 2020 involving allegations of childhood sexual abuse. The investigation also examined how some districts had resolved claims through confidential settlements, raising questions about transparency and public accountability.The newspaper reported that more than 330 cases had been settled for roughly $700 million at the time of its investigation, while the state projected that local education agencies could ultimately face payouts of between $2 billion and $3 billion as cases moved through the courts. The figures reflect a much wider set of claims across California and are not specific to ABC Unified.For school districts, cases of this nature can involve difficult questions about institutional responsibility: whether complaints were received, how they were investigated, whether employees were allowed to continue working with children and whether appropriate safeguards were put in place. In civil litigation, a district's potential liability can depend on what administrators knew or should reasonably have known and whether their response was adequate.The verdict may have concluded the jury's role in the first trial, but it has not brought the wider litigation to an end. With the settlement terms undisclosed and six other cases yet to be heard, questions surrounding the former teacher's alleged conduct and the district's response remain before the courts.
Article Summary: The plaintiff, identified in court-related publicity only as J.O., attended Luther Burbank Elementary School in Artesia, California. According to an announcement issued by his legal team at Herman Law, he alleged that he was sexually abused by a teacher when he was a child. The lawsuit accused ABC Unified School District of failing to protect students despite having prior notice of the teacher's alleged sexual misconduct involving other pupils.

Article Title: In 2011, two Los Angeles women began building Baby2Baby; 15 years later, it serves 1.5 million children a year and has distributed 850 million essentials, while its gala honouring Demi Moore raised a
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

An initiative that began as a small effort to get diapers and basic necessities to 500 children in Los Angeles has grown into a nationwide operation reaching 1.5 million children every year. Fifteen years after Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein took over and reshaped the nonprofit Baby2Baby, the organisation says it has distributed 850 million essential items across the US. Its milestone year culminated in a record-breaking gala that raised more than $20 million and honoured actor Demi Moore The 15th-anniversary celebration was held on November 14 at the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, California. The annual fundraiser brought together actors, musicians, philanthropists and supporters, with Moore receiving the organisation’s Giving Tree Award for her advocacy for children and families. Actor Andrew Garfield presented the honour, while singer Cardi B performed during the evening. The event was hosted by Keke Palmer. According to Forbes, the gala raised more than $20 million, marking the highest total in the event’s history.The money will support Baby2Baby’s work providing children and families experiencing poverty with essentials such as diapers, clothing, formula and emergency supplies.Baby2Baby was originally established in Los Angeles in 2006 as a grassroots initiative that collected and distributed gently used items for babies and young children. In 2011, Patricof and Weinstein took over the organisation, incorporated it and changed its mission to focus on providing new essentials to children in need. In an interview with Los Angeles Magazine, the co-CEOs recalled that they had been exploring ways to work together in the nonprofit sector when they began speaking to homeless shelters, children's hospitals and other community organisations. They repeatedly heard that families struggled to afford basic necessities, particularly diapers. The two women saw an opportunity to address a need that was often overlooked.At the time, Baby2Baby was a small volunteer-run operation. Patricof said it supported around 500 children in Los Angeles in 2011 and operated out of a tiny storefront on Pico Boulevard. Today, the organisation reaches approximately 1.5 million children annually across all 50 states and has warehouses across the country. Its workforce has also expanded from the two women and one intern to around 80 full-time employees, according to Los Angeles Magazine.The scale of its distribution reflects how central everyday essentials remain to its work. Over the past 15 years, Baby2Baby says it has provided more than 850 million items, including 400 million diapers. Its services reach families through nearly 1,000 nonprofit organisations and government agencies, including foster care agencies, schools, hospitals, homeless shelters, domestic violence programmes and disaster-relief groups.Diapers have remained one of its biggest priorities. The co-CEOs shared with Forbes that nearly one in two families in the US struggle to afford them. During the Covid-19 pandemic, when some parents were reportedly resorting to newspapers and towels as substitutes, the organisation began manufacturing its own diapers. Patricof told Los Angeles Magazine that this allowed it to produce them at around 80% less than retail prices and distribute more supplies.The organisation has also expanded beyond its original focus on children's everyday needs. Disaster relief has become a major part of its work, with Baby2Baby responding to more than 150 disasters over the past decade, according to the co-CEOs. Its assistance has included supplies for families affected by wildfires, hurricanes and floods. In 2026 alone, the organisation had responded to 30 disasters by the time of the anniversary gala.Another area of focus is maternal health. Baby2Baby's maternal health and newborn supply kits include diapers, wipes, hygiene products, breastfeeding supplies and postpartum care items. The initiative is intended to help mothers and newborns access essentials immediately after childbirth. The organisation told Forbes that the programme was being piloted in 21 states. It has also secured a $9 million investment from New York State to provide kits to 100,000 mothers giving birth on Medicaid across the state. In California, it has introduced a programme intended to provide 400 diapers to every baby born at participating hospitals.Despite the distribution figures and fundraising milestone, the organisation says demand continues to outstrip what it can provide. The co-CEOs said that Baby2Baby received requests for 1.9 billion diapers in 2026 alone, even though it has distributed 400 million over the past 15 years. They also said around 10 million children remain on its waitlist.For Moore, receiving the Giving Tree Award at the anniversary gala brought the focus back to the everyday challenges faced by parents. In her acceptance speech, she spoke about the reassurance of knowing that her children were safe and had what they needed while she built her career. She also highlighted the relief Baby2Baby can offer families who might otherwise have to choose between necessities such as food, rent and diapers.The record gala fundraising total marks a significant moment for Baby2Baby, but its leaders say the need for basic essentials remains far greater than the supplies already distributed.
Article Summary: Baby2Baby was originally established in Los Angeles in 2006 as a grassroots initiative that collected and distributed gently used items for babies and young children. In 2011, Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein took over the organisation and changed its mission to focus on providing new essentials to children in need. Over the past 15 years, Baby2Baby says it has provided more than 850 million items, including 400 million diapers. Its milestone year culminated in a record-breaking gala that raised more than $20 million and honoured actor Demi Moore.

Article Title: In 1981, Virginia recycled 7.85 miles of Route 220 into new asphalt using about 40% of the old road; two years later, the Franklin County pavement was performing well
Article Text:
AI Representation: Virginia recycled 7.85 miles of Route 220 into new asphalt using the old road. Image credits: Chatgpt

Virginia reused 40% of the old pavement on Route 220

Engineers modified an existing asphalt plant to process reclaimed material

A two-year evaluation found satisfactory pavement performance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hot mix asphalt being placed during road paving. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Road construction often involves removing damaged pavement and replacing it with new material. Engineers can also use recycled asphalt in order to create a new road surface as well. Virginia used this approach in three earlier projects in central Virginia, according to the Virginia Highway and Transportation Research Council, before it recycled a 7.85-mile stretch of US Route 220 in Franklin County in the fall of 1981. This project involved a 7.85-mile section of the road and included about 40% recycled pavement in the asphalt mixture. Engineers needed to evaluate whether used road material could be treated in a regular asphalt mixing plant and still serve under usual traffic conditions. The assessment conducted in 1984 confirmed that the used asphalt served quite well for about two years.The construction of Route 220 represented an extension of Virginia’s earlier efforts in asphalt recycling. The state had undertaken other hot mix recycling programmes prior to undertaking this major demonstration program. According to Hughes’s 1982 installation report, milling started on September 8, 1981, in the northbound lanes of US Route 220 in Franklin County.This was done because the base course of asphalt was in very good condition. Charles S. Hughes documented the construction process in the Virginia Highway and Transportation Research Council’s Installation Report : Evaluation of Recycled Hot Mix Asphaltic Concrete on Route 220, published in 1982. The report describes a project covering roughly 8 miles of roadway, where the top two asphalt layers were milled, recycled through a conventional batch plant and relaid. The finished mix used about 40% reclaimed material and 60% virgin aggregate and the work went ahead with little difficulty.The recovered asphalt was processed and incorporated into a new hot mixture. The final mix was 40% reclaimed pavement material and 60% virgin aggregate, which was a blend of granite and sand. About 3.0% AC-5 asphalt cement was added on top of that, as detailed in the research report. Hughes’s installation report says paving began on September 30 and was completed on October 28, 1981. The installation report says the project included the full width of both northbound lanes, from north of Rocky Mount to south of Boones Mill.The process involved the modification of an ordinary asphalt batch plant. Engineers included the installation of a bin and elevator to allow the transfer of the reclaimed pavement through the entire process. In addition, the materials went through a two-inch screen to eliminate the larger particles before going into the plant. In laboratory tests, the result indicated that the asphalt binder was highly rigid, especially the ones in the top layers of the pavement. This problem was sorted out by using softer AC-5 asphalt binder in the new mix. Finally, the project also resulted in the creation of excess materials beyond the needs of Route 220. Some of the excess materials were used for overlaying Route 40 in Franklin County. The initial use of cold recycled mix with CMS-2 emulsion was unsuccessful and therefore, the rest was done using hot recycled mix.Hughes examined the road’s condition in the 1984 report. Two-Year Evaluation of Recycled Hot Mix Asphalt Concrete on Route 220: Interim Report. The evaluation consisted of a comparison of the data collected during the construction of the road with those obtained one and two years after service. The characteristics of the asphalt did not vary much within the period. The air voids in the mixture decreased due to compaction or the sealing of the pavement by traffic. The surface texture increased slightly while the present serviceability index fell a bit. Skid resistance went up over the period of two years.The report stated that the recycled pavement had been doing well, two years after it had been laid. A later three-year assessment, Evaluation of Recycled Hot Mix Asphalt Concrete on Route 220: Final Report, published in 1985, reported very good pavement performance. These results also led Virginia to consider a specification for using up to 25% recycled materials in the manufacturing process of hot mix asphalt by contractors. Thus, the Franklin County case study was an example of successful use of reclaimed asphalt in the construction of highway pavements for several years.
Article Summary: Virginia recycled 7.85 miles of Route 220 into new asphalt using the old road. Engineers modified an existing asphalt plant to process reclaimed material. A two-year evaluation found satisfactory pavement performance. Some of the excess materials were used for overlaying Route 40 in Franklin County.

Article Title: In 1943, Army Airborne serviceman Jim Rudy recorded a voice letter for his wife; 74 years later, their daughter found the forgotten disc and heard his voice again
Article Text:
Seventy-four years later, a daughter hears her father’s voice again (representative image). Image Credits: ChatGPT

A message sent before the front line

A small disc, long forgotten among old family belongings (representative image). Image Credits: ChatGPT

Hearing him again

A wartime habit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Some family treasures turn up in very ordinary places. For Laurie Meyer, it was a small vinyl record buried with old family belongings. According to a 41 Action News report from KSHB, she was going through her family heirlooms when she found a recording of her father, Jim Rudy, that he had made during World War II . She had heard it once when she was a little girl, but she couldn't remember what it said. She wasn't sure if the audio could be saved.Rudy recorded the message in Chicago on 15 January 1943. At that time, he was in his early 20s and was soon to be sent to the European front lines as part of the Army Airborne. The message was addressed to his wife, June, who was Meyer’s mother. The disc was named ‘Love and Kisses – Jim.’ It later became a long-forgotten family relic. Meyer brought the record to Summit Video Services in Lee’s Summit, Missouri. She was hoping to hear her father's voice on the record. The team transferred the audio from the turntable and cleaned it using digital software. Chad Godfrey, the owner of the store, said that he had seen a World War II record like this just three times in 12 years of running his business. He told Meyer that the audio was perfect.Meyer was anxious to hear the recording. She listened to it with the KSHB team on a Thursday afternoon in March 2017.That was 74 years after it was recorded. The message ran about three minutes long. Rudy began by telling June that it was him remembering her. He hoped the little record would please her because it was different from writing. Meyer had warned that her father had a great sense of humour, and it showed in his words. He told June it would be easy to switch him off if she didn't like it. Yet the message was tender: “I am starving for your love and affection.” Near the end, he joked that his pizza had frozen to his trousers in the cold Chicago January. Then he said he was running out of words and out of record. He signed off by calling her “honey” and promising to write the next night again. For Meyer, it was an unbelievable experience to hear her father's young voice again. Meyer described her father as well-known and much loved. Godfrey called the disc an amazing souvenir and said it was satisfying to bring a piece of the past into the 21st century.Rudy’s record was also part of a wartime habit. The Smithsonian's National Postal Museum explains that the mail options increased in the 1940s to include recorded messages. Servicemen could use phonograph records to record their messages and mail them back home to their families. The American Philatelic Society , which is a non-profit organisation, mentions in an article written by Wayne Youngblood that Pepsi-Cola provided booths for servicemen to send their messages. Families loved these records, the article says, and played them again and again. Godfrey said both Coca-Cola and Pepsi ran promotions with booths like that.It wasn't all history for Meyer. It was about her father in his early 20s, making jokes about frozen pizza and missing his wife. It's a few minutes of fun and love captured just before he left for the front lines. Rudy died in 1990 in Overland Park. But now his young voice is saved, frozen in time forever, and Meyer says future generations of the family will share a part of it.
Article Summary: Laurie Meyer was going through her family heirlooms when she found a recording of her father, Jim Rudy, that he had made during World War II. Rudy recorded the message in Chicago on 15 January 1943. At that time, he was in his early 20s and was soon to be sent to the European front lines as part of the Army Airborne. The message was addressed to his wife, June, who was Meyer’s mother.

Article Title: Former Pakistan army officer is new BLA chief
Article Text:
BLA appoints ex-Pakistan Army Captain as chief (file photo)

In a major organisational shift, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has elevated its senior commander Rehman Gul to the post of commander-in-chief. Sources said his elevation carried symbolic weight given his past as a former captain in Pakistan army’s 19 Frontier Force (FF) Regiment.In 2010, Gul deserted the army, citing atrocities against civilians, and joined Aslam Baloch’s BLA, leaving the military brass flummoxed. Prior to assuming the top role, Gul served on the command council and led the Majeed Brigade, BLA’s operational wing which specialises in suicide bombings.Having graduated as a battalion senior major, Gul previously held military postings in Kotli in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir as well as North and South Waziristan, where he took part in military operations.The announcement also dispels earlier reports from the Pakistani military, which had declared Gul dead last year, a claim BLA didn’t validate. Adding a sensitive dynamic to the situation, sources indicate that Gul’s younger brother currently serves as a Major in the Pakistan army’s Signals Corps. Observers suggest that having a former military officer at the helm amplifies narratives of internal disillusionment among security personnel regarding state crackdowns and civilian casualties in Balochistan.The leadership transition, confirmed through a statement from group spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch on Nov 14, follows a unanimous vote by the outfit’s senior command council. The move comes just days after the announcement that Bashir Zeb was stepping down as chief.There was also uncertainty surrounding Zeb’s successor after the group said last week that Zeb was transferring all powers to the command council. While pro-Pak military social media accounts circulated rumours of Zeb having been poisoned by a confidante and being killed in Afghanistan, sources described them as false.
Article Summary: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) elevate senior commander Rehman Gul to the post of commander-in-chief. Gul is a former captain in Pakistan army’s 19 Frontier Force (FF) Regiment. In 2010, Gul deserted the army, citing atrocities against civilians.

Article Title: Redrawing Pakistan: Ministers back 12-province plan but political, constitutional hurdles remain
Article Text:
Pakistan's 12-province proposal gains momentum as senior ministers back restructuring (Representative Image)

What the proposed 12-province map could look like

Political consensus remains the biggest hurdle

What the Constitution requires

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan's proposal to expand its four-province structure to as many as 12 has gathered momentum, with senior ministers backing it in the name of better governance. But the idea faces a major political hurdle: there is no consensus among the country's leading parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh.Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif has argued that Pakistan's growing population requires smaller provinces that can deliver public services more efficiently. Speaking to Geo News, he said the country could consider creating 12 provinces, provided the boundaries were drawn on administrative rather than linguistic, ethnic or political grounds.“If there is a proposal for 12 provinces, then make it 12,” Asif said, adding that new units should not be created to serve “language, ethnicity or political interests”.Pakistan’s interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has also revived the debate, suggesting a referendum to gauge public opinion on the contentious issue. His remarks have fuelled speculation that powerful quarters favour a broader restructuring of Pakistan's administrative map, with reports pointing to a possible constitutional exercise in 2027.No formal roadmap, however, has been announced. The proposed number of provinces, their boundaries and the process for creating them remain undecided.One proposal reported in Pakistani media envisages dividing Punjab into four provinces, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan into three each, and Sindh into two. The plan could involve a nationwide referendum and a possible 28th Constitutional Amendment, although neither has been confirmed as an approved government initiative.Supporters argue that the existing arrangement concentrates too much administrative and financial authority in provincial capitals leaving smaller cities and districts dependent on decisions taken far away.Asif has questioned whether federal funds transferred to provincial governments are reaching local institutions, arguing that decentralisation could bring decision-making and resources closer to communities. Advocates of the proposal say smaller provinces would make public services more accessible and help address uneven development.But the debate is not only about the size of administrative units. It also raises questions about whether creating more provinces would improve governance without stronger local governments and greater financial autonomy for districts.The proposal has exposed differences within the ruling coalition itself. The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), led by Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, has firmly opposed any division of Sindh, while the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) has yet to settle on a formal position.The two parties are coalition partners in the federal government. The PML-N has said it will announce its position if the matter comes before Parliament, despite some of its leaders backing the creation of smaller provinces.A cabinet member in the Shehbaz Sharif government said reaching agreement would be difficult without the support of the major political parties.The issue has also prompted speculation about a possible understanding between the government and the main opposition, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). PML-N leader and former federal minister Khawaja Saad Rafique has suggested that the establishment could offer relief to jailed former prime minister Imran Khan in return for PTI's support for the proposed constitutional changes. There has been no confirmation of such a deal.Smaller parties have also entered the debate. The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has renewed its demand for new administrative units in Sindh, while Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain has called for new provinces to be considered through consultation and in the national interest.The Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party has backed the proposal on administrative grounds, while Jamaat-i-Islami has argued that the creation of new provinces should go hand in hand with strengthening local governments.Even if political parties agree on the broad idea, redrawing provincial boundaries would require a demanding constitutional process.Under Article 239 of Pakistan's Constitution, an amendment requires the support of at least two-thirds of the total membership of both houses of Parliament. If it changes the limits of an existing province, it must also secure the backing of at least two-thirds of the total membership of that province's assembly.That gives provincial parties considerable leverage over any proposed division.A nationwide referendum is not an automatic constitutional requirement for creating provinces. Any such exercise would need its own legal and constitutional basis, and Parliament could not simply be bypassed in deciding the process or framing the questions put to voters.Following a meeting between Pakistan’s president Asif Ali Zardari and prime minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday, a senior government official told news agency PTI that the two leaders had agreed to adhere strictly to the constitutional provisions governing the creation of new provinces. They also agreed that any proposed referendum would require parliamentary approval.Former federal information minister Muhammad Ali Durrani has meanwhile launched a campaign for the restoration of Bahawalpur province and the creation of 11 other smaller administrative units.For now, the proposal remains a subject of political debate rather than an agreed government plan. Any move to redraw the map would require agreement on boundaries, resources, parliamentary representation and the future of provincial institutions — as well as the constitutional numbers to make it happen.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif has argued that Pakistan's growing population requires smaller provinces that can deliver public services more efficiently. But the idea faces a major political hurdle: there is no consensus among the country's leading parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh.

Article Title: 24 militants, four soldiers killed in separate clashes in Pakistan's Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Article Text:
(Photo credit: IANS)

At least 24 militants and four Pakistani soldiers, including an army officer, were killed in separate encounters between security forces and militants in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces, the Pakistan Army said on Saturday, PTI reported.The army said security forces had carried out multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan since Friday, targeting militant hideouts in the areas of Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki.During an operation in Kolpur on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday, troops killed eight militants, including a suicide bomber, and recovered a large cache of weapons and ammunition, the military said.The army said the militants used armed quadcopters to target military vehicles on patrol. The attack killed Major Omer Minhas Nasir and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan.The Pakistani government last year designated terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as 'Fitna al Hindustan'. Islamabad has alleged that these outfits carry out terrorist activities at India's behest, but has not provided evidence to support the claim.In June, India criticised Pakistan at the United Nations over the use of the term, calling it "officially sponsored misinformation and disinformation dressed in religious terminology."Separately, security forces conducted operations against militant hideouts in Mir Ali, Datta Khel and surrounding areas of North Waziristan district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the military's media wing, 16 militants were killed in the engagements. Twelve were killed in an operation in Ali Khel, while two each were killed in Mir Ali and Datta Khel.Two soldiers, Havildar Asmat Ali and Naik Aftab Ali, were killed during the operations. The ISPR said both soldiers fought bravely and laid down their lives in the line of duty. It added that the operations had dealt a major blow to the militant network.Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the slain militants, who, according to the military, were involved in several terrorist activities, including the killing of civilians.Pakistan's federal government uses the term 'Fitna al-Khawarij' for militants belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
Article Summary: At least 24 militants and four Pakistani soldiers killed in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces. Security forces carried out multiple intelligence- based operations (IBOs) since Friday, targeting militant hideouts in the areas of Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki. During an operation in Kolpur on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday, troops killed eight militants.

Article Title: Pakistani teen mauled to death by tigress released from cage for TikTok video shoot

Pakistani teenager mauled to death after tigress freed for TikTok video in Lahore (Image source: X)

A 19-year-old Pakistani teenager was mauled to death by a tigress after it was let out of its cage for a TikTok video shoot.The victim, identified as Talha, was working at a private breeding facility in Kahna, Lahore district, when the animal attacked him. He was rushed to a private hospital but died while undergoing treatment on Wednesday, according to local reports.Police identified the arrested farm owner as Fayyaz and the TikToker as Noman. Investigators allege that the influencer had visited the property to film a video and asked for the animal to be released from its enclosure. The animal subsequently lost control and attacked the worker, police said.The incident also triggered an investigation into an alleged attempt to conceal the circumstances of the death. Police said efforts were made to portray the attack as an incident involving a dog rather than a big cat. The animal has since been handed over to wildlife authorities.Authorities are examining whether the farm had the necessary permits to keep the animal and whether adequate safety measures were in place at the facility. A case has been registered and investigations into possible negligence are under way.In a statement, Lahore Police said that the pursuit of social media content could not come at the cost of human life. It said all aspects of the alleged negligence and the attempt to conceal the attack would be investigated.There has been some confusion in initial media reports over whether the animal was a tiger or a lion. Lahore Police's statement described it as a tigress.

Article Title: Imran Khan-Asim Munir deal? Sisters' release from jail, hospital visit spark buzz in Pakistan
Article Text:
Release of Imran Khan's two sisters and his hospital visit fuel speculation of a possible political understanding with Pakistan's military establishment

PTI ready to make peace?

Nawaz Sharif , Benazir Bhutto precedent

Why a deal may not be straightforward

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Is Pakistan witnessing the first signs of a possible thaw between jailed former prime minister Imran Khan and the country's powerful military establishment? The release of two of his sisters and his recent hospital visit for eye treatment have come amid speculation that a political settlement involving Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir has taken place.His sisters, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi were released on Thursday from Lahore's Kot Lakhpat Jail after the Punjab government withdrew their extended detention orders. The two had spent 53 days in custody after being detained ahead of a Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) protest march. Their sister Aleema Khan remains behind bars.The release came a day after Imran Khan was taken from Adiala Jail to Islamabad's Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences for an eye examination and treatment. Doctors administered an injection for an issue affecting his right eye, besides treating his blood pressure. He was discharged in the early hours of Thursday and returned to prison.The developments have coincided with renewed speculation about a possible deal involving Khan and the military establishment. Pakistan interior minister Mohsin Naqvi, however, dismissed reports of any behind-the-scenes arrangement on Thursday, saying Khan and his family would receive whatever relief the courts granted them.The possibility of a rapprochement is not entirely new. In August, one of Imran Khan's closest aides, PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari, had told Reuters that the former prime minister would not confront the military if released."If Imran Khan was released tomorrow, hypothetically, he wouldn't do anything that would effectively damage the country," Bukhari had said, describing him as "magnanimous".He had also suggested that Munir could take the initiative to ease tensions, saying the army chief could extend a "healing hand" to the country."That doesn't mean you go loggerheads with the establishment, with the military leader," Bukhari said, adding that personal grievances could be set aside in the national interest.The remarks marked a notable shift in the PTI's public rhetoric after years of confrontation with the military establishment following Khan's ouster in a no-confidence vote in 2022.Bukhari, however, had mentioned that there were no talks between the PTI and the military. He also acknowledged that it was unclear whether Khan himself shared the willingness to reconcile being expressed by party leaders outside prison.The latest speculation has also been fuelled by opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai's claim in October that Khan could be facing pressure to accept an arrangement similar to those involving former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto.Sharif left Pakistan in 2000 after being ousted and imprisoned following the military coup led by General Pervez Musharraf. Bhutto spent years abroad in self-imposed exile after her government was dismissed in 1996.Achakzai alleged that the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz and Pakistan Peoples Party were part of a political arrangement that could pave the way for a similar outcome in Khan's case. However, he did not establish that any such agreement had been reached.An exile arrangement could potentially offer a way out of the prolonged confrontation, but there is no confirmation that Khan has agreed to leave Pakistan or that negotiations with Munir are under way.Imran Khan's relationship with the military establishment deteriorated after disagreements over key appointments and foreign policy. He has accused the military leadership, including Munir, of orchestrating his removal. The military denies interfering in politics.Despite being in prison since August 2023, Khan remains the central figure in Pakistan's political confrontation. His party continues to demand his release, access to family members and lawyers, and relief in the cases against him.The PTI's position also raises a crucial question: can its leadership outside prison negotiate or signal a compromise without Khan's explicit approval? Bukhari's August remarks came with the caveat that the former prime minister's own thinking might be different.For now, the signals remain contradictory. Two members of Khan's family have been released, he has received medical treatment, and a senior PTI aide has previously spoken of reconciliation. But the government has denied any political bargain, and there is no evidence of direct negotiations with Munir.Whether the latest developments represent isolated legal and medical decisions or the beginning of a fresh political opening remains the question.
Article Summary: Imran Khan's two sisters were released from jail on Thursday after 53 days in custody. He was also taken to a hospital for an eye examination and treatment. The developments have fuelled speculation about a possible deal involving Khan and the military establishment. Pakistan interior minister dismissed reports of any behind-the-scenes arrangement on Thursday.

Article Title: 74 militants killed in Pakistan security operations along Afghan border in 10 days
Article Text:
43 militants killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa raids, 31 in Balochistan operations: Pakistan

Pakistani security forces have killed 74 militants in a series of raids and operations in the country's northwest and southwest regions bordering Afghanistan over the past 10 days, the Associated Press cited military officials Friday.The raids were conducted in Mir Ali and Orakzai districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where troops killed 43 militants and recovered weapons, ammunition and explosive devices, the military said in a statement.Separately, security forces killed 31 militants in multiple operations in Balochistan province since November 3, the military said. The province has been witnessing a bloody insurgency led by the rebel Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).Kabul has denied accusations of providing support to militant groups operating against Pakistan.The Pakistani Taliban are a separate group from, but allied with, Afghanistan's Taliban, who returned to power in Kabul in 2021. Several TTP leaders and fighters are believed to be operating from sanctuaries across the Afghan border, a longstanding source of tension between Islamabad and Kabul.

Article Title: BLA claims 18 killed in suicide vehicle attack on Pakistan Army camp in Balochistan
Article Text:
Baloch Liberation Army claims responsibility for a suicide vehicle attack on a Pakistani Army camp in Balochistan, claiming 18 personnel were killed

NEW DELHI: Multiple casualties were reported in a VBIED attack at Pak army’s main camp in Mastung, Balochistan Thursday. The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) took responsibility for the attack, claiming to have eliminated 18 personnel.According to BLA, its Fidayeen attack, the Majeed Brigade, carried out an operation in the Kanak area of Mastung, targeting a Pakistani military camp with a suicide vehicle-borne improvised explosive device followed by an assault by its armed fighters who entered the premises and targeted military personnel.The attack unfolded while a meeting of senior Pak Army personnel including colonel rank officials was underway when the mini-truck laden with explosives rammed into the main gate of the camp.The area has been on the boil since Wednesday. According to pro-BLA accounts on Telegram, Pak security forces were carrying out “operation Radd-ul-Fitna”, aimed at destroying tunnels allegedly made by Baloch rebels, on Wednesday and Thursday in the area.They claimed to have destroyed seven tunnels and seized arms, ammunition and explosives. In Musakhel, unidentified set ablaze construction machinery and a separate explosion destroyed a bridge in Mastung.On Wednesday, 13 Pakistani police personnel including a Deputy Superintendent of Police were killed after fighters from the rebel group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) launched a major attack targeting mobile police units in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Article Title: 'Some good news': Two sisters of ex-Pak PM Imran Khan released from jail; elder sister, wife remain behind bars
Article Text:

Two sisters of Pakistan's incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan were released from a Lahore jail on Thursday after the Punjab government revoked their detention orders, leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) party said.However, his elder sister and wife remain behind bars."Finally, some good news. Two of former PM Imran Khan's sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, have been released from Kot Lakhpat Jail following the withdrawal of their detention orders," PTI senior leader and former federal minister Moonis Elahi said in a statement."Hopefully, Aleema sahiba and Bushra Bibi, will also be released soon," he added, referring to the cricketer-turned-politician's elder sister and wife, respectively.Meanwhile, another senior PTI leader, Zulfi Bokhari, asserted that the release of Imran Khan's two sisters would not "erase the suffering" endured by his family."The release of two sisters does not end the injustice or erase the suffering inflicted on Imran Khan’s family. The demand is clear -- no selective relief, no intimidation, and no further persecution," Bokhari told party supporters.Imran Khan's sisters were detained in September under a public safety law to prevent them from mobilising support for a nationwide protest demanding his release.Bushra Bibi was arrested in January 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced.The 74-year-old PTI founder has been in prison since 2023 and faces more than 100 cases, including corruption charges and allegations of inciting violence.On Wednesday, PTI lawyers met Imran Khan at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail to discuss his ongoing court cases, a day after the Islamabad high court directed authorities to facilitate the meeting.The lawyers spent four hours at the prison before leaving without speaking to the media.According to PTI lawyer Latif Khosa, who was part of the delegation, Imran Khan was experiencing problems with his blood pressure and eyesight.

Article Title: Pakistan announces schedule for Guru Nanak’s 557th birth anniversary celebrations despite Attari-Wagah closure
Article Text:
Pakistan has maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side (Photo: PTI).

AMRITSAR: Despite the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah international land border following Operation Sindoor, the Pakistan government has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev, expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib.Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side, although pilgrim movement through it continues to be suspended by India.According to Pak media reports, the programme was finalised at a meeting of the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (PSGPC), chaired by its president and Punjab provincial minister for minority affairs and human rights, Ramesh Singh Arora, to review arrangements for the celebrations.As per the schedule, Indian Sikh pilgrims are expected to arrive in Pakistan through the Attari international border on November 22. The main ceremony will be held on November 24 at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev. The pilgrims are scheduled to return on December 1.Reacting to Pakistan’s announcement, Sikh scholar Jagdeep Singh said the proposed pilgrimage programme assumes significance amid strained India-Pakistan ties and the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah border after Operation Sindoor.“Keeping the border open would serve the interests of both countries and, above all, make it easier for devotees to visit their historic religious shrines,” said Jagdeep.Interestingly, while Pakistan maintains that the Kartarpur corridor is operational on its side and has expressed readiness to facilitate Sikh devotees, India has suspended pilgrim movement through it since May 2025.In a statement, Arora said Pakistani diplomatic missions had been instructed to facilitate visa issuance for Sikh pilgrims. He also urged India to allow the Sikh sangat to visit its historic shrines.According to reports, the arrangements reviewed at the meeting include air-conditioned buses, accommodation, langar, medical facilities, mineral water and currency exchange services. A Rescue 1122 ambulance will accompany every convoy of 20 buses to meet medical emergencies.
Article Summary: Pakistan has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev. It is expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib. Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side.

Article Title: 'Two eight-year-olds or four four-year-olds': Pakistani cleric's child bride 'joke' sparks outrage
Article Text:
Mufti Tariq Masood (Source: Wikimedia Commons)

Education and women's autonomy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood, who commands a large following across social media platforms, has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage.In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.One of the remarks highlighted in the report came from a viral video in which Masood joked that if someone could not find a 16-year-old bride, he could provide “two eight-year-olds” or “four four-year-olds”. The comment drew criticism from people who said it trivialised child marriage and normalised the sexualisation of minors.The Daily Mirror said the backlash was dismissed by supporters as a misunderstanding, with the remark defended as a joke taken out of context.The newspaper also pointed to Masood's repeated opposition to statutory minimum marriage-age laws. According to the report, he has argued that Islamic jurisprudence does not prescribe a universal minimum age of 18 and that parents or guardians should retain discretion over when a girl marries.A recurring theme in his sermons, the newspaper said, is the emphasis on physical development and perceived maturity rather than chronological age when determining whether a girl is ready for marriage. The preacher had made remarks discussing the physical suitability of girls aged nine and ten in the context of marital relations. Pakistan as a country has been grappling with child sexual abuse, forced marriages and gender equality and positioning such leaders as popular figures raises extreme concerns.The Daily Mirror also highlighted Masood's remarks on women's education, saying that some of his statements appear to place a husband's authority above a young wife's decision to continue her studies.It further cited comments about women marrying late, including references to them becoming “aunties”, and discussions of the benefits husbands derive from marriage.Masood has also been criticised for presenting early marriage as a way to manage men's sexual desiresMasood's sermons have reportedly become difficult to access after copyright complaints and takedown requests. Critics have alleged that this limits public scrutiny of his statements, while his supporters maintain that some remarks are circulated without their original context.Masood has built a substantial following on YouTube, Facebook and other social media platforms through a preaching style that combines religious instruction with informal language and humour. His reach extends beyond traditional religious institutions, particularly among younger and urban audiences.
Article Summary: Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage. In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.

Article Title: Pakistan militant attack kills 10 policemen in KPK's Kohat, gunbattle still under way
Article Text:
No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. (FIle photo)

At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Wednesday, officials told news agency AP.The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire between the attackers and security forces, local police official Faisal Khan said.Khan confirmed that two senior police officers were among those killed. He added that the gunbattle was still underway, but did not share further details.No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. However, suspicion is likely to centre on the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, which has intensified its attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.Pakistan has witnessed a rise in militant violence over the past few years, with much of it attributed to the TTP. The group is separate from the Afghan Taliban but shares close ties with it. The Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.Islamabad has repeatedly accused Afghanistan's Taliban-led government of providing shelter to TTP fighters operating against Pakistan. Kabul has denied the allegations.
Article Summary: At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire. No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far.

Article Title: Bangladesh tensions rise ahead of Hasina's return; bomb blasts near Dhaka airport injure 3
Article Text:
The explosions took place on Monday night, with one bomb detonating near the airport's outer gate

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tensions are mounting in Bangladesh ahead of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina 's planned return next month, with a series of arson attacks and incidents of violence prompting heightened security across the country. Adding to the concerns, two crude bombs exploded near Dhaka's Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Monday night, injuring three pedestrians, as authorities stepped up measures to prevent possible political unrest.The explosions took place on Monday night, with one bomb detonating near the airport's outer gate and another in the Jasimuddin area, close to the airport and connecting flyovers, the Dhaka Tribune reported on Tuesday, quoting police.Kamrul Islam Talukdar, officer-in-charge of the Airport Police Station, said miscreants had thrown the bombs from a flyover, causing minor injuries to three pedestrians. Security arrangements have since been strengthened.The blasts come amid renewed tensions over Hasina's possible return in December. The former prime minister, who fled to India in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government, recently sought a new passport and national identity card, signalling preparations for her return.Bangladesh has witnessed several incidents of violence in recent days, including arson attacks targeting trains, buses and banks. Police have blamed Awami League activists and members of affiliated organisations for some of these incidents. The party has been barred from political activities and elections following Hasina's removal from power.Amid fears of further unrest, law enforcement agencies have drawn up special security plans for Dhaka, Gopalganj and other Awami League strongholds, Bengali daily Prothom Alo reported. Additional police personnel will be deployed throughout December, while intelligence surveillance has been stepped up nationwide.Security has been particularly tightened in Gopalganj, Hasina's home district, which has witnessed incidents of arson and vandalism. Around 2,000 police personnel have been deployed there, along with 10 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh and Special Response Battalion personnel.Meanwhile, Hasina faces serious legal challenges at home, including a death sentence handed down in absentia by a special tribunal over the deadly crackdown on protesters during the 2024 uprising. She has denied wrongdoing and questioned the legitimacy of the proceedings.Bangladesh has also sought her extradition from India. New Delhi has acknowledged receiving the requests but has not announced a decision.
Article Summary: Two crude bombs exploded near Dhaka's Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Monday night, injuring three pedestrians. The blasts come amid renewed tensions over Hasina's possible return in December. The former prime minister, who fled to India in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government, recently sought a new passport.

Article Title: Dhaka denies India set conditions for Hasina’s return
Article Text:

DHAKA: State minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaid Islam on Monday said Bangladesh expects former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina , who has been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity, to be brought back from India under the existing extradition treaty, dismissing reports of possible conditions attached to her return.“This report has no basis. It did not originate from a responsible source within the Indian government. Anyone could publish such a report. Ultimately, a report like this means nothing,” she told reporters at the ministry of foreign affairs, noting that if an official communication were to come from India - specifically from their Ministry of External Affairs or the Indian government itself – they would certainly receive it and provide a response.“Beyond that, we have neither the time nor the inclination to concern ourselves with what is being published elsewhere in India; it is simply not our business,” she said.On the other hand, independent MP Rumeen Farhana has said she could see inconsistencies in statements made by ministers and an adviser to the prime minister regarding the intended return of Hasina.She said the relationship between Bangladesh and India is far broader than just Sheikh Hasina.“The relationship is not confined to this single issue. We do have issues, but we will resolve them through our diplomatic channels. I think we are making this far more important than it needs to be,” she said, noting that Bangladesh currently has many other issues to discuss - the government is engaged in a great deal of work, and there are numerous matters that deserve their attention beyond this.“I would ask: why wouldn’t India make use of the extradition treaty? The treaty exists. Any accused individual - they all fall into the same category. They could all be brought back under the provisions of the extradition treaty. If India were to respond in this regard, it would make things easier for the people of Bangladesh, as well as for the government of Bangladesh,” she told reporters while responding to a question at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has written to India multiple times under the extradition treaty," she said, adding that the Ministries of Law and Home Affairs are examining the legal and technical aspects of the matter.Shama said the government believes Hasina, like any other accused persons, should be brought back under the treaty to serve her sentence.“Simply being a citizen of Bangladesh does not guarantee that you will be issued a Bangladeshi passport – if you are a convicted criminal, if you are implicated in cases involving crimes against humanity,” she said.Responding to reports that India had set two conditions for Hasina's return, including providing her an opportunity to appeal and restarting her trial, the State Minister said the reports have no basis in Bangladesh's laws.“No, not at all. We have had no such conversations with them on this matter,” she said, making it clear that Bangladesh had received no such official proposal from India as reported by BBC Bangla.Shama said Bangladesh-India relations are much broader than the issue of Hasina, stressing that the two neighbouring countries have longstanding ties and several important bilateral issues that need to be addressed through diplomacy.“Bangladesh-India relations are a much bigger deal than Sheikh Hasina,” she said, urging against making the issue appear more important than it needs to be."We have issues. We will deal with the issues through diplomacy," Shama said.However, she said the government cannot ignore Hasina's activities in India if they are aimed at destabilising Bangladesh.On the Bangladesh-India Consular Dialogue, originally scheduled for November 17-18, Shama said the meeting had not been cancelled but deferred to a mutually convenient time.She described reports suggesting that the meeting had been cancelled as misinformation, saying both sides agreed that it would be better to hold the talks later when the respective sides are available.The State Minister also indicated that Bangladesh would host several high-level foreign visits in the coming days, although she did not disclose any names or tentative dates.Asked whether water-sharing issues, particularly the Ganges water issue, were discussed at a meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Shama said the government could hold extensive discussions with the Prime Minister on a range of issues.She, however, did not directly confirm whether the Ganges water issue was discussed at the meeting.The State Minister said, “We have not forgotten the history of petrol bombs. The acts of arson and destruction that took place in the past were carried out by the Awami League, and the arson and destruction happening now are also being carried out by the Awami League - this is a proven fact. This terrorist organization is doing exactly what it has always done. And when such a terrorist group operates from another country - a nation with which we have relations and with which we need to foster stronger ties - then, as the government of Bangladesh, it is certainly our responsibility to address this. ”
Article Summary: Shama Obaid Islam says Bangladesh expects former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to be brought back from India under the existing extradition treaty. She dismisses reports of possible conditions attached to her return. She says Bangladesh-India relations are much broader than the issue of Hasina, stressing that the two neighbouring countries have longstanding ties.
